items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had not heard too many trumpet players except Dolly and Dyer Jones, Sydney de Paris, John Nesbit, Freddie Jenkins and the fellow from New Orleans that played around town on a wagon.

ctx.x: When I was 14 years old, we moved to Hathaway Street which was in the back of Kenyon Avenue. I never missed a show in the Lincoln Theatre and

eventually a trumpet player came to Cincinnati and was engaged to play at the Lincoln with Amanda Randolph. His name was John Nesbit and he made quite a name for himself as a trumpet player later, and as an arranger also. He stayed in Cincinnati for quite sometime and he was the best trumpet or cornet trumpet player of all those I heard before him. When Nesbit did leave town it was to join McKinny's Synco Septet.

One day while playing in front of my house with some of the other boys, we saw some young people going down the street and there were two women who had trumpet cases with them and later we heard music coming from a house further down the street. We stopped whatever we were playing and went in front of this house in order to hear the music better. Those sessions happened many times and I was always around to hear them from outside.
